transcript.content: Hello, I'm glad you could make it in today. What brings you in to see me?

Well, I suppose I'm here because things have been pretty tense at home lately. For the past year, I've been noticing some patterns with my wife. She says the late meetings and these little changes in her work messages are just normal office stuff, but... well, they just line up too precisely to feel accidental. It really seems like there’s some kind of private signal in them, like they're meant to tell me something she won’t just say directly. It's been weighing on me and causing some friction, so I figured I should come in and talk about it.
Have you ever heard voices, sounds, or whispering when no one else was around?

No, no I haven't. I don't hear voices or whispering or anything like that. It's really just the things I'm seeing, you know? The messages, the schedules, the actual things happening right in front of me. But no, no sounds or voices when I'm alone.
Over the past year, have you been experiencing persistent feelings of sadness, low mood, or a loss of interest in things you usually enjoy?

No, not really. I mean, I'm stressed, obviously, because of everything going on with my wife. It's frustrating and it takes up a lot of my mental energy. But I wouldn't say I'm sad or depressed. I still go to work, I still do my job as a TA, I still like watching the game on weekends. It's just... this whole situation with her is a lot to deal with. But my mood overall is fine.
Have you ever had the feeling that your thoughts were being read, broadcast out loud, or put into your head by an outside force?

No, definitely not. My thoughts are my own. I've never felt like anyone could read my mind or put thoughts into my head. Like I said, it's just the stuff I'm actually seeing—the emails, the schedules. It's all real things happening on the outside, not anything going on inside my head.
Outside of this situation with your wife, have you generally found it difficult to trust friends, coworkers, or other people throughout your life?

No, not at all. I've always gotten along fine with people. I trust my coworkers at the university, and I have a solid group of friends. I've never really been a suspicious person or had trouble trusting people in general. 

It's really just... well, this specific situation with my wife, because of the actual evidence I've seen. But normally? No, I trust people just fine.
